scope: Bounded discovery of Ireland’s national free-movement and family-residence routes, EEA EFTA and Swiss treaty distinctions, UK Withdrawal Agreement rights, visa entry and mission guidance, registration, administrative procedure and remedies, public access, privacy, oversight, legal aid, and courts. Ireland is an EU Member State but is not part of the Schengen area. This is not a legal-equivalence opinion or complete national inventory.
retrieval_status: 26 original captures and 26 derived candidate conversions are hash-verified and indexed in the Monitor local-only archive; 11 eISB legislative texts are accepted under documents/legislation; 15 other conversions remain archive-only; 25 sources are link-only; 51 official reference links are accepted within scope.

comparison_seed.source: Danish EU-residence regulation and official guidance used as the comparison seed
comparison_seed.relationship_note: SI 548/2015 is a close functional source because it gives effect to Directive 2004/38/EC for Union citizens and their family members. Ireland’s own text refers non-EU EEA citizens to earlier instruments; Swiss rights arise through the EU–Swiss agreement and Irish domestic effect; UK Withdrawal Agreement and Irish-national family routes are distinct. Similar function does not establish legal equivalence.

previous_findings_carried_forward: Denmark remains the comparison seed; prior Denmark-to-Sweden and Finland findings, and Austria’s broad statute with an EEA-specific cluster, were carried forward as search leads only.

The source taxonomy review identified gaps beyond residence statutes: procedures, file access, consular instructions, family-status evidence, remedies, privacy, oversight, legal aid and court decisions. These classes were searched separately.

N-Lex is a useful EU Member State legislation discovery route, as seen in prior country reviews, but its links and search results are leads; national identity and current text must be verified at eISB or another first-party publisher.
Czechia’s keyless date-bound PDF route and Estonia, Finland and France’s documented structured-data routes are adapter examples only; none establishes an Irish API or reuse permission.

Greece’s unresolved portal terms showed why access rights must be checked for the actual publisher and endpoint. Ireland’s eISB publishes an Open Data PSI licence, but that licence is not assumed to cover other Irish authority websites.
Prior findings are not evidence that Ireland has an equivalent source, a current text, or complete source-class coverage.
